title: Quickstrike engineer scripts and fallback lattice (draft)
content:
Purpose:
A compact, field-friendly set of one-liners, contextual troubleshooting steps, and a decision lattice for SEs to run during pilot calls, live demos, and urgent post-sale escalations. Focus is on fast resolution, clear fallback choices, and communicating tradeoffs (latency / cost / quality) to customers in a single breath.

Audience:
Sales Engineers, Solutions Engineers, Platform Sellers, Pilot Engineers, Customer Success 1:1s. Not intended as an exhaustive ops runbook — this is the quickstrike pack you pull up during a call.

How to use:
- Open this doc in the call, copy the short script lines.
- If you need deeper diagnostic logs, jump to the "Diagnostics" section and file JIRA if persistent.
- For canary/fallback decisions, follow the lattice (bottom of doc) and call out the customer-visible behavior change.

Quick open scripts (1-2 sentence)
- "If latency spikes >200ms p50 after an auth change: check region routing — ping the example endpoint and confirm region header. If wrong region, toggle the 'Region override' in the console to match customer's VPC. Sample: curl -H "x-region: us-west1" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/predict"
- "If model hallucination on structured outputs: switch to the vetted quantized variant (qa-small-xxq) and reduce temperature to 0.0 for deterministic rerankers. Phrase: 'We'll switch to our strict-output profile that'll lock the output schema and reduce creative tokens.'"
- "If throughput drops under commit: verify batch window and autoscale policy (console -> Dedicated -> throughput). Quick CLI check: rwdctl pools describe --pool-id <id>"

Objection rebut snippets (short)
- Cost too high: "We can prioritize prefix/KV caching and a low-latency fallback model. That reduces tokens and cost by ~35% in most document summarization pilots."
- Can't tolerate outages: "We use model-variant fallthroughs and multi-region canaries — customers keep read-only fallbacks while we failover to Dedicated pools."
- Security/compliance: "Private can be deployed in your VPC with customer KMS and audit logs retained per your retention policy."

Common diagnostics (3-minute checks)
1) Verify routing & region: curl the health endpoint with x-region header; confirm host resolves to correct VPC VIP.
2) Check request/response token counts: console -> traces -> sample -> token_breakdown; flag if > expected by 2x.
3) Model mismatch: check model_version in headers; if not pinned to requested hash, explain rollout policy and offer to pin.

Escalation quickfire (what to say to the customer, and what we do internally)
- Customer message: "We see this behavior and will schedule an immediate canary to validate a fallback option; you shouldn't lose traffic — we'll keep your previous model pinned until verification."
- Internal steps (SE -> Solutions Eng -> SRE): collect sample request id, timestamp, trace link, include short reproduction and environment (host, region, model_variant).

Fallback lattice (decision flow summary)
- Symptom: High latency or error rate
  1) Is degradation isolated to one region? -> Yes: reroute to nearest healthy region (manual region override), monitor for 10m.
  2) Global impact? -> Check Dedicated pool health; if Dedicated degraded, switch traffic to hosted variant with pinned model and reduced batch size.
  3) If model-level quality regression only -> rollback model version or switch to a conservative variant (e.g., dynamic -> static kv cache).

Model mapping cheat sheet (for quick verbal mapping)
- Production accuracy, mid cost: redwood-std-1 / quantized-std-1q
- Low-cost fallback (latency-first): redwood-lite-0.5q
- Strict-schema deterministic: redwood-qa-0

Canary checklist (for on-call SE to run in 15 minutes)
- Pin the old model for 5-10% traffic and scale new model to 0% initially.
- Run 200 synthetic requests covering edge prompt set (attach prompt file).
- Compare token and latency distributions; if latency delta < 15ms and error delta < 0.5%, expand rollout.

SE language examples (plain talking points)
- For execs: "We're optimizing for predictable unit economics — we'll route to the variant that meets your latency SLO while keeping accuracy within your tolerance band."
- For engineers: "Here's the single curl to validate region and the trace id pattern — if you paste the id in Slack we'll review logs with you in real time."

Open questions / items to refine (notes-to-self)
- Add explicit curl examples for auth headers used in Private deployments.
- Create a short deck slide that visualizes the fallback lattice (diagram + 3 example failures).
- Validate claims: caching reduces token cost by ~35% — get a metric from Optimize team for legal/marketing copy.

Appendix: quick copy-paste snippets
- Validate region: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "x-region: us-west1" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health | jq .region
- Pin model API sample: curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"route":"my-route","model":"redwood-std-1","pin":true}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/admin/routes/pin
- Basic throughput check (CLI): rwdctl metrics tail --route my-route --window 5m

Version notes:
- v0.1 (2025-11-12): initial draft, SE field-tested in three pilots (fintech, HR automation, support summarization).
- v0.2 (2026-02-15): added canary checklist, added mapping cheat sheet, added linked artifacts.

If you're using this on a call: copy two items into a private Slack note (diagnostic + fallback choice) so we can iterate the lattice quickly after the call.

TODOs (short):
- Convert this doc into a 1-slide printable "quick card" for SEs
- Add two real examples (anonymized) with before/after metrics
- Coordinate with Optimize to get verified % cost savings and update the rebut scripts

End of doc.
